proposed_features.description: The primary type of movement performed by the subject: swimming strokes, diving, or cliff jumping. This distinguishes between continuous swimming motions and discrete jumps into water.

The pattern of arm motion during the activity: alternating, simultaneous, or no visible arm motion. This helps differentiate between front crawl (alternating) and breaststroke (simultaneous) versus diving (no swimming motion).

Whether the head is above water, submerged, or alternately lifted during the activity. This distinguishes breaststroke (head lifts) from front crawl (head submerged) and diving (head down during entry).
The manner in which the subject enters the water: vertical dive, horizontal jump, or splash from swimming. This separates diving and cliff diving from swimming strokes.
The type and intensity of disturbance on the water surface: large splash, small ripple, or minimal disturbance. This reflects the force and angle of entry, distinguishing diving from swimming.
The setting in which the activity occurs: indoor pool, outdoor pool, natural cliff, or structured diving platform. This helps distinguish between controlled environments and natural settings.
Whether a diving board or springboard is visible and used. This is specific to diving activities and absent in swimming or cliff diving.
The height of the subject above the water surface at the start of the action: high (cliff), moderate (diving board), or at water level (swimming).
The duration of the main action from start to end: short (diving/cliff jumping) or long (swimming). This reflects the time spent in motion.
The orientation of the body during the action: horizontal (swimming), vertical (diving), or angled (cliff jumping). This helps distinguish between swimming and diving.
Whether lane lines or pool markers are visible, indicating a structured swimming environment. This is common in swimming but not in cliff diving or casual diving.
The position of the subject relative to the camera: side view (swimming), top-down (diving), or front-facing (cliff diving). This reflects camera angle and activity type.
